children: A worsening economic outlook for China next year may compel policymakers to respond with more aggressive stimulus measures, says Julius Baer China strategist Richard Tang in an email. This could lead to a sustained recovery in the equity market sometime in 1H27, Tang notes. Southbound investors have been net selling Hong Kong stocks for three consecutive weeks, while onshore Chinese mutual funds are still heavily positioned in AI infrastructure, with limited room for further buying, he adds. The Chinese market went up sharply after the Democrats' victory in the U.S. Congress. Investor positioning and market narrative are the real drivers of the rebound, he says. The aggressive rebound in China's internet stocks are a result of the normalization of positioning, Tang says. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
